info.title: Brainitive App API
info.description:
The JSON API of the first-party **Brainitive Desktop** and **Brainitive Mobile** apps. Every
Brainitive server (Brainitive Cloud or self-hosted) serves it under `/api/v1`.

It is separate from the MCP server, the CLI and the browser extension: own tokens, own guard, own
rate limits. Conventions (full text in `docs/ai/API.md` of the repository):

- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer bra_...` - a 15-minute access token from the native sign-in
  (`/app/authorize` in the system browser -> `POST /auth/exchange`). Refresh with
  `POST /auth/refresh` (`brr_...`, 60 days, single use; replaying an old one revokes the device).
  Tokens of the MCP / CLI / extension clients get 401 here.
- **Errors:** always `{"message": "...", "code": "...", "errors"?: {"field": ["..."]}}` - 401
  `unauthenticated`, 403 `forbidden`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `conflict`, 422 `validation_failed`,
  429 `rate_limited`. A 404 can also mean "exists, but not for you".
- **Dates:** ISO-8601 UTC.
- **Lists:** cursor pagination `?cursor=&limit=` (default 50, max 100) -> `{data, next_cursor}`;
  `updated_since` for sync.
- **Writes:** `Idempotency-Key` accepted; updates carry `revision` / `updated_at` -> 409 on conflict.

Rotate the token pair. The refresh token works once; presenting an already-used one again
signs the whole device out (reuse = a stolen copy) and emails the user. Clients must send
one refresh at a time: two parallel refreshes with the same token count as reuse

appToken.description: Access token from POST /auth/exchange or POST /auth/refresh. 15 minutes; refresh before it expires. Passport tokens (MCP / CLI / extension) are rejected.

current.description: the device of the calling app token; always false on the web Profile page

ExchangeCodeRequest.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/exchange: the one-time code from brainitive://auth/callback, the PKCE
verifier and the device that signs in. Whether the platform fits the client is checked after
the code is known (AuthController::exchange).
ExchangeCodeRequest.title: ExchangeCodeRequest

can_accept.description: a member accepting just closes the invitation (same as the web)

slug.description: only members learn the slug before accepting; the app opens it right away

email_verified.description: true also when the instance does not require verification (User::hasVerifiedEmail)

timezone.description: null until a browser or app sent one; effective_timezone is what reminders use

billing_url.description: "Plan & billing" on the web; null on self-hosted installs

icon.description: an emoji or the URL of an uploaded icon

role.description: the user's project role; null for workspace admins who aren't project members

create_issues.description: one board answers for all: createItems depends only on the project role

recently_updated.description: the project page's "Recently updated" (a board / list / helpdesk counts when its content changed)

type.description: board | list | plan | helpdesk | lead_form | page

summary.description: what it sets up: counts per section (boards, docs, lists, plans …)

version.description: the saved version of a workspace template; null for built-in ones

RefreshTokenRequest.description: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh: the current refresh token (`brr_…`, single use).

refresh_token.description: anything longer than our tokens is answered as an invalid grant, not a validation error

RefreshTokenRequest.title: RefreshTokenRequest

StoreProjectRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/projects` (BRAI-389): the web form's rules (ProjectCreator).
Authorized before validation, so somebody outside the workspace gets a 404 and can't probe which
names or keys are taken; members who may not create projects get a 403. A retried template
run (same `request_id`) skips validation, which would fail on "name already taken", and the
controller answers with the project the first request created (as the web form does).

template.description: Start from a template: "builtin:<key>" or "template:<uuid>" (see TemplateRuns::catalog)

items.description: "none" stands for "nothing extra" (an empty array isn't sent by forms)

StoreProjectRequest.title: StoreProjectRequest

StoreWorkspaceRequest.description:
A new workspace: the web form (WorkspaceController::store) and the apps' first run
(POST /api/v1/workspaces). Names are unique per owner among their live workspaces.
StoreWorkspaceRequest.title: StoreWorkspaceRequest

UpdateAvatarRequest.description: `POST /api/v1/me/avatar` (BRAI-384): multipart `avatar`, the web Profile page's image rules.
UpdateAvatarRequest.title: UpdateAvatarRequest

UpdateDeviceRequest.description:
PATCH /api/v1/devices/current: the calling app updates what it knows about itself (after an
update, a rename, or once it has a push token). Only the sent fields change; a null push_token
removes it.

push_token.description: APNs device token / FCM registration token; stored encrypted, never returned

UpdateDeviceRequest.title: UpdateDeviceRequest

UpdateMeRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/me` (BRAI-384): the fields the web Profile page edits, each optional. Same rules
as the web (ProfileUpdateRequest). The email address is web only: a new one must be verified.

timezone.description: all_with_bc: browsers still report old names such as "Asia/Calcutta".

UpdateMeRequest.title: UpdateMeRequest
